title: Gebhard von Dollnstein-Hirschberg becomes Pope Victor II
description: The German-born Gebhard became head of the Catholic Church and ruler of the Papal States, succeeding Pope Leo IX, who had died in 1054. Victor II was one of a series of German-born popes who led the Gregorian Reform; he died in 1057.

title: Otto II marries the Byzantine princess Theophanu
description: The sixteen-year-old co-emperor married the fourteen-year-old Theophanu, niece by marriage of Emperor John I Tzimiskes, and the pope crowned her empress. The match sealed a marriage and peace agreement between the Ottonians and the East.

title: The first American abolition society is founded in Philadelphia
description: The Society for the Relief of Free Negroes Unlawfully Held in Bondage was founded in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, and held four meetings. Seventeen of the 24 men who attended its first meetings were Quakers, members of the Religious Society of Friends.

title: Lincoln calls for militiamen to suppress the Southern rebellion
description: President Abraham Lincoln signed Proclamation 80, calling for 75,000 militiamen to suppress the rebellion in the states of the Confederacy. Those Southern states had seceded from the Union to preserve slavery; the conflict became the American Civil War.

title: Ormonde's Royalist army defeats the Irish Confederates at Kilrush
description: In the Battle of Kilrush a Royalist army under the Earl of Ormonde routed Irish Confederate troops commanded by Lord Mountgarret. The Irish Confederate Wars, begun with the rising of 1641, caused an estimated 200,000 deaths.

title: Emperor Otho takes his own life after his defeat at Bedriacum
description: Otho, the second emperor of the Year of the Four Emperors, ended his three-month reign by suicide after Vitellius defeated him at the Battle of Bedriacum. The Roman Senate recognised Vitellius as emperor on 19 April.

skip: The article gives 16 April without a year, right after Agatho's death in January 681, and dates only the consecration (17 August) to 682: the election year is not clear.

title: Harald Hen dies and his brother Canute IV takes the Danish throne
description: Harald III, king since 1076, who had sought to replace trial by combat and ordeal with sworn oaths, was buried at Dalby Church in Scania. His brother and successor Canute IV was slain by rebels in 1086 and became the first Danish king to be canonized.

title: Virginia's secession convention votes to leave the Union
description: Three days after the seizure of Fort Sumter, the Virginia Secession Convention voted to secede, on condition that a referendum approve it the next month, and to join the Confederacy. Northwestern counties loyal to the Union went on to form West Virginia.

title: Congress proposes counting slaves as three-fifths of persons for tax
description: A proposed amendment to the Articles of Confederation would have taxed the states by population, and Congress settled on counting slaves by the three-fifths ratio proposed by James Madison. It failed, two states short of the unanimous approval required.

title: The University of Alabama opens its doors to students in Tuscaloosa
description: Established by the state's General Assembly in 1820, the university opened with Alva Woods as president and around 100 students a year in the 1830s. William Nichols designed its campus around a domed Rotunda that served as the library.

title: Confederate sympathizers attack Union militia in Baltimore
description: On Pratt Street, Confederate sympathizers fought Massachusetts and Pennsylvania militia on their way to Washington. The riot produced the first deaths of Union volunteers by hostile action in the American Civil War; attackers were killed too.

title: Charles V agrees the Truce of Frankfurt with the Protestants
description: At Frankfurt-on-the-Main, where Philip Melanchthon represented the Lutherans, the emperor promised no violent action against the Schmalkaldic League for fifteen months from 1 May. As a result of the peace, the League lost the protection of France.

title: Baldwin III takes sole control of Jerusalem from his mother Melisende
description: After besieging Queen Melisende in the Tower of David, Baldwin III had become master of Jerusalem by this date, and she retired to Nablus under a negotiated settlement. He began his sole rule by giving the government offices to his trusted partisans.

title: Alaungpaya's men wipe out a Hanthawaddy detachment at Halin
description: Alaungpaya led forty of his best men against a 50-man Hanthawaddy detachment at Halin, south of Shwebo, and wiped it out, in the first resistance of the Konbaung–Hanthawaddy War. The war ended the Mon people's centuries-long dominance of the south.

title: Babur defeats and kills Ibrahim Lodi at the First Battle of Panipat
description: Babur's 24,000 men, armed with muskets and artillery, defeated the 100,000-strong army of Ibrahim Lodi, Sultan of Delhi, who died on the field with 20,000 of his men. The battle ended the Lodi dynasty and began Mughal rule in India.

title: The Wignacourt Aqueduct begins carrying water to Valletta
description: Built by the Order of Saint John to bring water from springs in Dingli and Rabat to the new capital Valletta, the aqueduct was inaugurated after work resumed in 1610. Named after Grand Master Alof de Wignacourt, it stayed in use until the 20th century.

skip: A sports first (the first National League baseball game): trivial for a history site.

title: Settlers race into the Unassigned Lands of Oklahoma at high noon
description: The first land run into the Unassigned Lands of the former Indian Territory started, with an estimated 50,000 people lined up for two million acres. The land had been assigned to the Creek and Seminole peoples since the 1830s.

title: The Boston Latin School is established in Massachusetts
description: The school was established in Boston, Massachusetts, and is the oldest public school in the United States. It remains a Latin grammar school today, a magnet state school of the city of Boston.

title: Nicholas I, later called Nicholas the Great, becomes pope
description: Nicholas I became bishop of Rome and leader of the Papal States a week after the death of Benedict III, and held the office until his death on 13 November 867. He is the last of the three popes listed in the Annuario Pontificio with the title "the Great".

title: The Boston News-Letter publishes its first issue
description: The Boston News-Letter is regarded as the first continuously published newspaper in the colony of Massachusetts. Heavily subsidized by the British government and of limited circulation, it printed only copies the Royal governor had approved.

title: A Dutch fleet destroys the Spanish fleet in the Bay of Gibraltar
description: During the Eighty Years' War a Dutch fleet surprised a Spanish fleet anchored in the Bay of Gibraltar, and in four hours of action most of the Spanish ships were destroyed. The war was a revolt of the Habsburg Netherlands against the Spanish government.

title: The Bourbon army wins the Battle of Almansa
description: In the War of the Spanish Succession an army loyal to Philip V of Spain defeated one supporting his Habsburg rival, Archduke Charles of Austria. The decisive Bourbon victory reclaimed most of eastern Spain for Philip.

title: France and Scotland renew the Auld Alliance at Corbeil
description: The Treaty of Corbeil bound each kingdom to join the other in declaring war if either was attacked by England. The Scottish deputation of King Robert the Bruce was led by Thomas Randolph, 1st Earl of Moray; France was ruled by Charles IV.

title: Sybil Ludington's ride is said to rally militia near Danbury
description: Relatives later claimed that the 16-year-old daughter of Patriot colonel Henry Ludington rode 40 miles through the night to rouse militiamen after British forces burned Danbury, Connecticut. Scholars largely reject the story.

title: Emperor Arcadius marries Aelia Eudoxia, daughter of Bauto
description: The 17-year-old emperor of the East married Eudoxia, daughter of the Frankish general Bauto, in a match arranged by the eunuch Eutropius against the plans of the prefect Rufinus. Her rise showed the shifting centres of power at the eastern court.

title: Miguel de Benavides founds the University of Santo Tomas in Manila
description: The Spanish friar Miguel de Benavides, third Archbishop of Manila, founded the university, which holds the oldest extant university charter in Asia. Run by the Order of Preachers, it is one of the largest Catholic universities by enrollment on one campus.

title: Gonzalo Fernández de Córdoba defeats the French at Cerignola
description: Outside Cerignola in Apulia, a Spanish force of around 9,000 men with 1,000 arquebusiers defeated a French army of 9,000, whose commander Louis d'Armagnac, Duke of Nemours, was killed. It was one of the first European battles won by small arms fire.

title: The Crown of Castile completes the conquest of Gran Canaria
description: After a five-year war, Castile under Queen Isabella I took Gran Canaria from the Canarii who had long lived there, and the Canarian queen Abenchara was captured and imprisoned. The conquest was an important step in the expansion of a unified Spain.

title: Gustav Vasa's Swedish troops defeat a Danish force at Västerås
description: On Badelundaåsen, northeast of Västerås, Swedish troops led by Gustav Vasa defeated a Danish force under Didrik Slagheck and took the town. Their war deposed King Christian II from the Swedish throne and effectively ended the Kalmar Union.

title: Enguerrand de Marigny is hanged on the gibbet of Montfaucon
description: Arrested by Louis X at the instigation of Charles of Valois, the chamberlain and minister of Philip IV was condemned on a charge of witchcraft. He protested that he had only carried out Philip's commands; his body stayed on the gallows until 1317.

title: The Territory of Orleans joins the Union as the State of Louisiana
description: The Territory of Orleans, organized on October 1, 1804, was admitted to the Union as the State of Louisiana, the 18th U.S. state. Reflecting its French heritage, Louisiana is the only U.S. state whose political subdivisions are termed parishes.

title: A council at Carthage condemns the teachings of Pelagius
description: Bishops met under Aurelius of Carthage to act against the errors of Caelestius, a disciple of Pelagius, and denounced Pelagian doctrines of human nature, original sin, grace and perfectibility. The council fully approved the contrary views of Augustine.

title: James II's forces defeat the Black Douglases at Arkinholm
description: At Arkinholm near Langholm, a small action of only a few hundred troops decided the civil war between King James II and the Black Douglases, the most powerful noble family in Scotland. The win was a step towards a strong centralised Scottish monarchy.

title: Llywelyn the Great has William de Braose hanged
description: The Marcher lord, captured by Llywelyn in 1228, had begun an affair with Llywelyn's wife Joan while in captivity, and was caught with her at Easter festivities in 1230. Llywelyn had him hanged; the Welsh had called him Gwilym Ddu, Black William.

title: Nerio Acciaioli's troops take the Acropolis, ending Catalan Athens
description: Besieged since 1385, the Catalans surrendered the Acropolis to the Florentine Nerio I Acciaioli, ending Catalan rule in Athens. Nerio made Greek the language of government and let the Orthodox archbishop settle in the lower town.

title: The largest of a series of earthquakes strikes Rhodes
description: The earthquake struck at 3:00 in the morning and triggered a small tsunami that caused local flooding; an estimated 30,000 people died. It was the largest of a series of earthquakes on Rhodes from March 1481 to January 1482.

title: The Kongo king Nzinga a Nkuwu is baptised as João I
description: Portuguese priests baptised the ManiKongo, who took the name João in honour of Portugal's King João II, and his principal nobles were baptised too. He abandoned the new faith in 1495, partly because the Church required monogamy.

title: The Council of Constance declares John Wycliffe a heretic
description: The council banned Wycliffe's writings and decreed that his works be burned and his remains removed from consecrated ground. The order, confirmed by Pope Martin V, was carried out in 1428, when his corpse, or a neighbour's, was exhumed and burned.

title: The Swedish rebel leader Engelbrekt Engelbrektsson is murdered
description: Engelbrekt, who had led the rising of 1434 against Eric of Pomerania, was killed on an islet in Lake Hjälmaren by the nobleman Måns Bengtsson, whose father had a legal dispute with him. Over the next decades he became a Swedish national hero.

title: The Second Council of Constantinople opens
description: Convoked by Emperor Justinian I under Patriarch Eutychius, the fifth ecumenical council sat until 2 June. Of the 152 bishops, only sixteen came from the West, none of them from Italy; it is recognised by the Eastern Orthodox and Catholic Churches.

title: Mary Dixon Kies becomes the first woman awarded a U.S. patent
description: President James Madison signed her patent for a new technique of weaving straw with silk and thread to make hats. It was the first United States patent awarded to a woman.

title: Konbaung armies storm the starving city of Pegu
description: After a siege that left the city starving, Konbaung forces broke into Pegu at moonrise and massacred men, women and children. Alaungpaya entered through the Mohnyin Gate, the walls were razed, and the fall ended the Konbaung–Hanthawaddy War.

title: Work begins on Bangkok's Grand Palace for King Rama I
description: Rama I, founder of the Chakri dynasty, ordered the palace built when he moved the capital from Thonburi to Bangkok. It has been the official residence of the kings of Siam since 1782, and the court and government were based there until 1925.

title: Constantius Gallus arrives at Antioch as Caesar of the East
description: Gallus, appointed Caesar by his cousin Constantius II at Sirmium in March, reached his capital Antioch. Around this time the Jews of Palestine revolted under Isaac of Diocaesarea, a rising that Gallus's general Ursicinus later put down.

skip: The material (a lead only) names the two forces at Vrtijeljka near Cetinje but not the outcome or what followed.

title: Columbus sails from Cádiz on his fourth and last voyage
description: Columbus left with his flagship and three other vessels, crewed by 140 men, among them his brother Bartholomew as second in command and his son Fernando. The Catholic Monarchs had agreed to fund the voyage after restoring his freedom and wealth.

title: Temür is enthroned as the second emperor of the Yuan dynasty
description: Temür, known by his temple name as the Emperor Chengzong of Yuan, reigned until 10 February 1307. He is counted as the sixth Great Khan of the Mongol Empire, though only nominally, as the empire was divided; his reign set the patterns of power for decades.

title: Agapetus II becomes pope as the nominee of Alberic II of Spoleto
description: Alberic II, princeps of Rome from 932 to 954, controlled the papacy and appointed the five popes after John XI, among them Agapetus II. The new pontificate fell in the period known as the Saeculum obscurum.

title: Edgar and Ælfthryth are consecrated king and queen at Bath
description: King of the English since 959, Edgar was consecrated with his wife Ælfthryth on Whit Sunday; the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle implies it was a first coronation, though historians debate whether it was a second. Only English magnates attended.

title: Minnesota becomes the 32nd state of the United States
description: Minnesota Territory had been formed in 1849, and its founding population was so largely of New England origin that the state was dubbed "the New England of the West". Treaties with the eastern Dakota and Ojibwe gradually forced them onto reservations.

title: Trajan's Column is dedicated in Rome
description: The triumphal column in Trajan's Forum commemorates the emperor's victory in the Dacian Wars, and its spiral bas relief depicts the wars between Romans and Dacians. It was probably built under the architect Apollodorus of Damascus at the order of the Senate.

title: Stephen I becomes bishop of Rome in succession to Lucius I
description: Stephen I succeeded Lucius I, who had died on 5 March 254, and held office until his death on 2 August 257. He was later canonized, and some accounts say he was killed while celebrating Mass.

title: Agapetus I becomes bishop of Rome after the death of John II
description: Agapetus I succeeded John II, who had died on 8 May 535, and held office until his death on 22 April 536. His father Gordianus was a priest in Rome, and he may have been related to two popes, Felix III and Gregory I.

title: Settlers on the Cumberland River sign the Cumberland Compact
description: Some 256 settlers led by James Robertson and John Donelson signed the compact near the French Lick, providing for a government and a system of justice. There they built Fort Nashborough, which later became Nashville, Tennessee.

title: The First Crusade lays siege to Seljuk-held Nicaea
description: The siege of Nicaea, the first major battle of the First Crusade, lasted until 19 June. Fearing that the crusaders would break in, the Seljuk Turks holding the city chose to surrender it to the Byzantines.

skip: The article gives this day only for the election of Uriah Tracy as president pro tempore of the Senate; it does not mention the recess or the move to Washington.

title: Princes crush Thomas Müntzer's peasant army at Frankenhausen
description: On the second day of the battle, troops of Landgrave Philip I of Hesse and Duke George of Saxony defeated the peasants under their spiritual leader Thomas Müntzer. It was the final act of the German Peasants' War in Thuringia.

title: Thado of Mohnyin enters the capital of Ava unopposed
description: After a slow, deliberate advance that let King Nyo's vassals desert him, Thado bribed the Sagaing commander to leave the fight, and Nyo and Queen Bo-Me fled. Thado entered Ava without resistance and took the throne four days later.

title: Militia and Regulators clash at the Battle of Alamance
description: The battle near Great Alamance Creek in colonial North Carolina was the final confrontation of the Regulator Movement. The Regulators had demanded reform of the Currency Act, an end to the corruption of local politicians and a right to secret ballot voting.

title: Liberius becomes bishop of Rome after the death of Julius I
description: Liberius succeeded Julius I, who had died on 12 April 352, and was consecrated on 22 May according to the Catalogus Liberianus. He is the earliest pope not venerated as a saint in the Roman Martyrology; he died on 24 September 366.

title: Adrian III becomes pope two days after the death of Marinus I
description: Adrian III, or Hadrian III, became bishop of Rome and leader of the Papal States after Marinus I died on 15 May 884. In little more than a year in office he worked to help the people of Italy in a time of famine and war; he died on 8 July 885.

title: The Ottoman Empire begins the Great Siege of Malta
description: Ottoman forces attempted to conquer Malta, then held by the Knights Hospitaller, in a siege that lasted nearly four months, until 8 September 1565. The attempt failed.

title: An earthquake devastates Shanxi around Linfen
description: The shallow magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck Shanxi Province in North China under the Qing dynasty and affected over 120 counties across eight provinces. An estimated 52,600 people died, although the death toll may have been 176,365.

title: John II of Castile defeats the Infantes of Aragon at Olmedo
description: Castilian forces defeated those of Navarre and Aragon outside Olmedo, in the First Battle of Olmedo. The Infantes of Aragon were the sons of Ferdinand I of Aragon, among them Juan, King of Navarre and later King John II of Aragon.

title: The Prome kingdom surrenders to Toungoo after a five-month siege
description: With starvation in the city and its allies from Ava and Mrauk U defeated by Bayinnaung, King Minkhaung of Prome surrendered and was taken to Toungoo with his queen. Tabinshwehti made Prome a provincial capital again.

title: Mohnyin Thado formally ascends the throne of Ava
description: The 46-year-old took a long regnal title and made his 15-year-old eldest son heir apparent; his soldiers marked the coronation by sacrificing horses and cattle to the Mahagiri spirit. Senior princes had not given up their claim to the throne.

title: The Picts defeat and kill King Ecgfrith of Northumbria at Dun Nechtain
description: The Picts under King Bridei son of Beli defeated the Northumbrians, and Ecgfrith, who had ruled Northumbria at the height of its power, lost his life. Bridei's reign saw a strong Pictish state form north of the Forth.

title: The collapse of a lava dome on Mount Unzen sets off a deadly tsunami
description: Volcanic activity of Mount Unzen brought down the Mayuyama lava dome and a tsunami followed. Approximately 15,000 people died, the largest volcanic disaster in Japanese history; many of the dead were in Higo.

title: Michael IX Palaiologos is crowned co-emperor at Hagia Sophia
description: Patriarch John XII of Constantinople crowned the eldest son of Emperor Andronikos II, who had declared him emperor before 1282. Andronikos went on to entrust Michael with wars against the empire's internal and external enemies.

title: Lü Bu kills the warlord Dong Zhuo at the palace gate
description: Encouraged by Interior Minister Wang Yun, Lü Bu, sworn to Dong Zhuo as a son, struck the fatal blow at the palace gate in Chang'an. Dong's death is seen as a destabilizing event in the collapse of the Eastern Han and a precursor to the Three Kingdoms wars.

title: A strong earthquake shakes Istanbul and the Sea of Marmara
description: The magnitude 7.1 earthquake, centred in the eastern Sea of Marmara, struck in the early hours and was felt from Izmit to Rodosto, where a tsunami followed. It was the last major earthquake to strike Istanbul from the North Anatolian Fault.

title: The Second Virginia Charter enlarges the London Company's grant
description: The charter gave the London Company adventurers a say in the company's policies and granted it land stretching "from Sea to Sea", 200 miles north and south of Cape Comfort. It named some 650 investors who had subscribed to the colonization effort.

title: President Paredes of Mexico issues a manifesto against the United States
description: Mariano Paredes issued the manifesto a month after his declaration of a defensive war on 23 April; some consider either the de facto start of the Mexican–American War. The Mexican Congress declared war officially on July 7, 1846.

title: John Brown and his men kill five pro-slavery settlers in Kansas
description: After pro-slavery forces sacked Lawrence, Brown and a band of abolitionist settlers abducted and murdered five pro-slavery settlers near Pottawatomie Creek in Kansas Territory, in the night of May 24–25. A teenage son of one settler was spared.

title: Bosphorus yamaks kill a minister and rise against Selim III
description: Yamaks refusing the uniforms of the Nizamı Cedit killed Raif Mehmet, the minister of the Bosphorus, and marched on Constantinople under Kabakçı Mustafa. Selim III had to abolish his reforms and resigned, or was forced to, on 29 May.

skip: A single accidental explosion (the Mobile magazine), of the kind left out as trivial for a history site.
A local celebration (A Great Jubilee Day in North Stratford): trivial for a history site.

title: Lincoln signs the act creating the Montana Territory
description: President Abraham Lincoln signed the law organizing the Territory of Montana, an organized incorporated territory of the United States. It lasted until November 8, 1889, when it was admitted to the Union as the 41st state.

title: Dorgon and Wu Sangui defeat Li Zicheng at Shanhai Pass
description: At the eastern end of the Great Wall the Qing prince-regent Dorgon, allied with the former Ming general Wu Sangui, defeated Li Zicheng, founder of the Shun dynasty. The victory let the Qing army take Beijing and led to Qing rule in China proper.

title: The infant Richard III is anointed Prince of Capua
description: The only son of Robert I of Capua, under the regency of his uncle Jordan, died within a few months. No contemporary chronicler blames Jordan, but some modern historians doubt his innocence; he succeeded to the throne unopposed.

title: Cathars kill the inquisitor William Arnaud at Avignonet
description: A small force made up mainly of Cathars massacred a group of inquisitors, the Dominican William Arnaud and eleven of his companions, during the Albigensian Crusade. Count Raymond VII of Toulouse probably connived at the killing.

title: Prince Rupert's Royalists storm the Parliamentarian town of Bolton
description: In the First English Civil War Royalist forces under Prince Rupert stormed and took the town. It was alleged that up to 1,600 defenders and inhabitants were slaughtered; the massacre at Bolton became a staple of Parliamentarian propaganda.

skip: The article dates the Antioch earthquake only to late May 526, "probably between 20 and 29 May": the day is uncertain.

title: Paul I succeeds his brother Stephen II as pope
description: A former Roman deacon, Paul I had often served his brother Stephen II in negotiations with the Lombard kings. He led the emerging Papal States until his death on 28 June 767.

title: The Fatel Razack lands the first indentured Indian labourers in Trinidad
description: The ship had left Calcutta on 16 February with 225 immigrants and landed them in the Gulf of Paria. It was the first ship to bring indentured labourers from India to Trinidad; the day of landing is marked as Indian Arrival Day.
